facts.note: Transcript gives the same watch reading (twenty minutes to nine) at the temple's nine strike at dinner, and the uncle's scene about it.
Félix goes to the library alone after dinner, and his watch shows twenty to ten when the temple strikes ten.
Thump in the atelier at eighteen minutes past ten by his watch, followed by the repeater: ten slow deep notes counted, then doubled notes, then quick high ones he did not count.
Someone goes quickly up past the library door at a quarter past ten by his watch, before the thump. Someone comes quickly down at twenty-one past ten. He did not see who; the door was shut.
When the thump came, his aunt's piano was still playing downstairs.
Bastien Girard comes into the library at thirty-two minutes past ten by his watch, and they sit together until the temple strikes eleven.

added.quote: I had been looking at the clock on the library mantel, and I thought it was earlier than I expected.
added.why: Introduces a second clock in the library (the mantel clock) and implies it disagrees with the watch's reading at the ten o'clock strike, so the watch and the mantel clock may not match.

added.quote: I was alone on the floor directly below his atelier, drinking my uncle's brandy while he sat upstairs with his repeater.
added.why: Places the uncle in the atelier during the period after dinner while Félix was drinking in the library, which the sheet does not cover before the ten o'clock thump.
